content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "no", "applies_why": "The judge does not rest only on a verse's failure to state the link, because it names Matthew 1:16, 18, and 20 as the verse or phrase settling the withholding of the active begetting verb.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "The text states that before Mary and Joseph came together she was found with child of the Holy Ghost ([L1] Matthew 1:18, 20), with the active begetting verb withheld from Joseph in the record of the generations ([L2] egennēthē in Matthew 1:16).", "rule_words": "A verse that admits both readings is such a verse. It is not, if the judge names another verse or phrase that settles it.", "room": "I interpreted the exception another verse or phrase that settles it to require a specific named verse or phrase beyond the bare non-statement; I weighed whether Matthew 1:16 egennēthē with Matthew 1:18 and 20 is such a settling phrase, and concluded it is.", "why": "The judge names Matthew 1:16, 18, and 20 as the settling verse or phrase, so the K-S2 exception applies and the non-statement is not an impermissible ground."}
